title: ActivityLog tracks one busy row, so a second Undo re-arms the first mid-flight
body:
## Summary ActivityLog keeps a single `busy` id for every row's Undo, so starting a second undo re-enables the first row's button while its server action is still running, and the first one's `finally` clears the second's "Undoing…" early. A failed undo's reason also appears with no live region. ## Description `examples/demo-kit/src/activity/ActivityLog.tsx:67` holds `busy` as one `number | null`; `:76` sets it per click and `:87` clears it in the shared `finally`. `:127` disables a row only while `pending && busy === entry.id`, so after row B is clicked, row A's button is live again although A's `onUndo` has not returned; a second press on A sends a second undo, which the server answers `#A was already undone` and `:83` paints as A's error even though A succeeded. The failure line at `:114` is a plain `

` with no `role="alert"`/`aria-live`, so a screen-reader user who pressed Undo hears nothing when it fails. Fixed looks like: a `Set` of in-flight ids (add on click, delete in that call's own `finally`), each row disabled while its id is in the set, and the error line in a polite live region. ## Flow - the template's /activity page lists two reversible rows (examples/demo-kit/template/app/activity/page.tsx:17) - press Undo on row A, then on row B before A's server action returns - busy becomes B: row A's button reads "Undo" and is enabled again while A is still in flight - press A again: a second undoAction(A) runs and A shows "#A was already undone" as an error - A's finally sets busy to null: row B stops reading "Undoing…" while B is still running ## Expected impact Anyone undoing two rows quickly (the template's activity page; any app that adopts the shared log) sees a success reported as an error and a button that lies about being idle; measured by a DOM test that clicks two rows with a held promise. A Set-based busy state could break nothing that renders today, since only the template mounts this view. ## Evaluation Claim: user - each row's Undo is disabled exactly while its own undo is in flight, and a failure is announced Before: walked: two overlapping undos leave row A enabled mid-flight and clear row B's pending label when A settles; the error

has no live region (ActivityLog.tsx:67,76,87,114,127) After: predicted: row A stays disabled until its own call settles, row B keeps "Undoing…" until its own, a second press on A is impossible, the reason is read out Method: simulation - the race needs two clicks against held promises; this round built a static render instrument (ui-webmcp.test.ts load hook) but the kit has no DOM (jsdom/happy-dom are not dependencies), so no click can be fired Result: better Gate: none
instrument: a DOM test (add happy-dom as a demo-kit devDependency, or reuse ui-webmcp.test.ts's .tsx hook with react-dom/client over a DOM shim): render two reversible rows with onUndo returning held promises, click A then B, assert A's button stays disabled and B's label survives A settling; red today

title: The activity log cuts at its limit and never says how many it left out
body:
## Summary
`listActivity` returns the newest N rows with no total, and `ActivityLog` renders them as the whole history, so the template's activity page silently stops at 100 entries.

## Description
AGENTS.md: "Announce truncation. Any bounded output carries (showing N of M)." `examples/demo-kit/src/activity/index.ts:91-95` runs `SELECT * FROM activity ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT ?` and returns only the rows; no count travels with them. `examples/demo-kit/src/activity/ActivityLog.tsx:92-136` renders whatever it is handed with no footer, and `examples/demo-kit/template/app/activity/page.tsx:9` passes `listActivity(db(), 100)` under a lede that says "Every mutating action lands here". After the 101st action the oldest rows vanish with nothing on screen saying so. Fixed looks like: `listActivity` returning the kit's own `Bounded<ActivityEntry>` (`{ showing, of, items }`, webmcp/bounded.ts), or a `countActivity(db)` beside it, and `ActivityLog` taking an optional `total` and printing "Showing 100 of 312" when they differ.

## Flow
- an app logs its 101st action (logActivity, activity/index.ts:61)
- the activity page calls listActivity(db, 100) and gets rows 312..213 with no total
- ActivityLog renders 100 rows and no footer; the page's lede promises every action
- proposal: count the table in the same read, hand the total to ActivityLog, render the footer only when cut

## Expected impact
A reader of the provenance strip (the demo's audit view) learns the log is partial instead of concluding an old action never happened; measured by a db test over 101 rows plus a render test of the footer. Breaks nothing if `total` is optional; tidycrm's tests call `listActivity(db(), 1)[0]` and would need the shape change only if the return type changes.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the activity view says when it shows fewer entries than exist
Before: listActivity returns rows only; ActivityLog has no total prop; 0 of 1 activity views announce a cut (activity/index.ts:91-95, ActivityLog.tsx:48-57)
After: predicted: 1 of 1 - with 101 rows and limit 100 the view renders "Showing 100 of 101"; with 3 rows, no footer
Method: simulation - the change touches the template's activity page (the demo-kit-template context's file, swept concurrently) and possibly tidycrm's tests, so it is out of this round's paths; the render and db instruments exist in ui-webmcp.test.ts
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: ui-webmcp.test.ts: openDb on a temp file, log 101 entries, assert the read reports of=101 showing=100; render ActivityLog with total=101 and 100 entries and assert the footer text; red today (no total exists)

title: An Undo toast disappears after four seconds whatever the reader is doing
body:
## Summary
`ToastProvider` dismisses every toast on one 4 s timer, including a toast that carries an Undo action, with no pause on hover or focus, so a keyboard user can lose the button (and their focus) while reaching it.

## Description
`examples/demo-kit/src/ui/Toast.tsx:50-55` schedules `dismiss(id)` after `ttlMs` (default 4000) for every toast. `examples/hirelane/components/board/useRun.ts:59` puts an Undo on its toasts, so the one control that reverses an act has four seconds to be reached by Tab from wherever focus is; when the timer fires the focused button unmounts and focus falls to <body> (WCAG 2.2.1 Timing Adjustable, 2.4.3 Focus Order). The whole stack is also one `role="status" aria-live="polite"` region (`Toast.tsx:64`), so an `error` toast waits behind whatever is being read. Fixed looks like: a toast with an action does not expire while the pointer is over the stack or focus is inside it (pause and resume the timer), a longer floor for action toasts, and error toasts in an assertive region.

## Flow
- hirelane: an act lands and useRun shows a success toast with Undo (useRun.ts:59)
- a keyboard user starts tabbing toward the toast at the bottom-right of the page
- 4000 ms after it appeared the toast is dismissed (Toast.tsx:54), the button unmounts mid-reach or under focus
- focus drops to <body>; the act can no longer be undone from the toast

## Expected impact
Keyboard and screen-reader users of the three apps that share ToastProvider get the Undo the others get; measured by a fake-timer DOM test that focuses the action and advances 10 s. A paused timer could leave a toast up indefinitely if focus is stranded, so the pause must end on blur.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - an action toast cannot expire while the reader is on it, and an error is announced promptly
Before: walked: every toast, action or not, is dismissed at 4000 ms regardless of hover/focus; one polite region for all tones (Toast.tsx:54,64; caller useRun.ts:59)
After: predicted: with focus inside an action toast at t=10 s it is still mounted; it expires ttl after blur; an error toast is in an assertive region
Method: simulation - the behaviour is timers plus focus, which needs a DOM and fake timers; the kit has no DOM dependency and this round's render instrument is static only
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: a DOM + fake-timer test of ToastProvider (happy-dom devDependency): toast with an action, focus its button, advance 10 s, assert still mounted; blur, advance ttl, assert gone; error tone lands in an assertive region; red today

title: open_group's miss lists groups as a bare array; its sibling tools bound them
body:
## Summary
In `useZoomTools`, `open_group`'s failure reply returns every group id as a plain array, while `read_view` and `open_item`'s failure reply use the kit's one bounded envelope.

## Description
`examples/demo-kit/src/webmcp/bounded.ts` exists so every list a tool returns has one shape, `{ showing, of, items }`, and AGENTS.md says any bounded output announces its cut. `examples/demo-kit/src/webmcp/zoomTools.ts:114` bounds the groups in `read_view` and `:166-167` bounds `open_item`'s `available`, but `:132-136` returns `available: spec.groups().map((g) => g.id)` unbounded and unenveloped. An agent that learned the envelope from `read_view` reads `open_group`'s `available` as a different type, and a surface with more than `PAGE` (40) groups would hand back all of them. Fixed: `available: bounded(spec.groups().map((g) => g.id))`.

## Flow
- an agent calls open_group with a stale id
- zoomTools.ts:132-136 answers { ok: false, error, available: [ ...every id ] }
- the same agent's open_item miss answers available: { showing, of, items } (zoomTools.ts:166-167)
- proposal: wrap open_group's list in bounded() so all three listings share the envelope

## Expected impact
An agent driving any of the four zoom surfaces parses one shape for every list; measured by the count of zoomTools listing sites using `bounded` (2 of 3 today). Hirelane's group count (roles x stages) is the largest today and stays under 40, so no reply is cut today; the change alters a failure reply's shape only.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - every list a zoom tool returns uses the one bounded envelope
Before: 2 of 3 listing sites in zoomTools.ts use bounded() (lines 114, 167; line 135 does not)
After: predicted: 3 of 3; open_group's miss returns available: { showing, of, items }
Method: simulation - the handlers are closures inside useWebMCPTool calls; calling one needs a React client render (no DOM in the kit) or extracting the handlers into a pure builder, which is the instrument
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: extract the four handlers into an exported pure `zoomToolHandlers(spec)` that useZoomTools registers, then a test calling open_group with an unknown id and asserting `available` has showing/of/items; red today

title: Kit README lists a useWebMCPTool option and a bounded field that do not exist
body:
## Summary
`examples/demo-kit/README.md`'s signatures list `available?` on `useWebMCPTool` and a `footer` on `bounded`'s result, and its prose promises a `(showing N of M)` footer; the code has none of the three.

## Description
`examples/demo-kit/README.md:187` lists `useWebMCPTool({ ..., deps?, available? })`; `WebMCPToolSpec` (`examples/demo-kit/src/webmcp/hooks.ts:40-56`) has no `available`. `README.md:190` gives `bounded(items, cap): { showing, of, items, footer }`; `Bounded<T>` (`examples/demo-kit/src/webmcp/bounded.ts:23-29`) is `{ showing, of, items }`, and its docblock explains the English sentence was deliberately replaced by numbers. `README.md:57-58` says the shape comes "plus a `(showing N of M)` footer". An app author following the README passes an option that is silently ignored (or fails typecheck) and looks for a field that is never there. Fixed: drop `available?`, give `bounded(items, page?, project?)` / `boundedPage(items, page, size?, project?)` with `{ showing, of, items[, page] }`, and say the count IS the announcement.

## Flow
- an app author reads README section Signatures to register a tool
- passes `available: false` per README:187 - TypeScript rejects it (excess property) or, untyped, it is ignored
- reads a tool result's `footer` per README:190 - undefined
- proposal: correct the three lines from the exported types

## Expected impact
Whoever copies the template to start a new host app gets an API description that matches the code; measured by the count of README signature members absent from the exported types (3 today). Nothing can break; it is prose.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - every member the README signature lists exists on the exported type
Before: 3 documented members with no implementation (README.md:57-58 footer prose, :187 available?, :190 footer)
After: predicted: 0
Method: simulation - README.md belongs to no context in context-map.json and is outside this round's write set; a doc-parity test (README signature keys vs WebMCPToolSpec / Bounded keys) is the S instrument
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: a test reading README.md's Signatures block and asserting each listed useWebMCPTool key is a key of WebMCPToolSpec and bounded's listed fields equal Object.keys(bounded([]))

title: Five of the kit's six runtime dependencies are imported by nothing
body:
## Summary
`@athena/demo-kit` declares `@ag-ui/client`, `@ag-ui/core`, `rxjs`, `zod` and `class-variance-authority` as dependencies, and no file in the kit, its template or its tests imports any of them.

## Description
`examples/demo-kit/package.json` lists six runtime dependencies; a grep for an import of each over `examples/demo-kit` finds `clsx` in 7 files and the other five in 0. No other package in the workspace declares them, so nothing relies on them arriving through the kit either. They have been declared since the kit landed (3d41193), and the kit now describes itself as having "no chat, no provider and no runtime" (`webmcp/index.ts:2-3`), which is the kind of code these packages serve. They are installed for, and audited against, every app that depends on the kit. Fixed: remove the five from `dependencies` and refresh `pnpm-lock.yaml`.

## Flow
- pnpm install resolves @ag-ui/client, @ag-ui/core, rxjs, zod, class-variance-authority for the kit
- git grep for an import of each under examples/demo-kit: 0 files (clsx: 7)
- proposal: drop the five from examples/demo-kit/package.json, pnpm install to update the lockfile, run every example's typecheck and tests

## Expected impact
Smaller install and audit surface for the four example apps and the journey e2e; measured as declared-but-unimported runtime deps, 5 today. Could break an app that imports one of them undeclared through hoisting; the grep finds none, and the example gates would show it.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - every runtime dependency the kit declares is imported
Before: 5 of 6 declared runtime dependencies have 0 importing files in examples/demo-kit (git grep, this round)
After: predicted: 0 of 1 unused (clsx only), all example gates green
Method: probe - the import count is measured; the removal needs a lockfile refresh (a shared surface outside this round's paths, and an install that may reach the network), so the After is not taken here
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
$ for d in @ag-ui/client @ag-ui/core rxjs zod class-variance-authority clsx; do git grep -l "from \"$d" -- examples/demo-kit | wc -l; done
@ag-ui/client 0
@ag-ui/core 0
rxjs 0
zod 0
class-variance-authority 0
clsx 7
$ grep -ln '@ag-ui|"zod"|"rxjs"|class-variance-authority' examples/*/package.json apps/*/package.json packages/*/package.json
examples/demo-kit/package.json
instrument: remove the five from examples/demo-kit/package.json, `pnpm install --offline` (lockfile), then pnpm typecheck and every example's test; a seeded check: re-add an import of zod in a kit file and watch typecheck fail to resolve it

title: The kit's HostManifest types mirror manifest.py by hand, unpinned and unused
body:
## Summary
`HostManifest`, `ManifestTool` and `ManifestReadable` in `webmcp/types.ts` restate the README section 3.3 contract (`src/athena/contracts/manifest.py`) by hand, have no parity test and no consumer, and already lack four fields the real manifest carries.

## Description
AGENTS.md: "never fork a contract type inside a package". `examples/demo-kit/src/webmcp/types.ts` declares the manifest types and `examples/demo-kit/src/index.ts:21-25` exports them, but `git grep` finds no import of any of them outside the barrel. The shape the bridge actually builds (`packages/athena-bridge/gate.js` `manifestOf`, and `HostManifest.from_dict`) carries `page_origin`, `origin_kind`, `transport_detected` and per-tool `inferred_from`, none of which the TS types have; until this round's b76fb2b, `ManifestTool.side_effects` was typed in the kit's `data` vocabulary the contract rejects. Either delete the three types (nothing reads them) or pin them to manifest.py with a parity test like `tests/test_refusal_parity.py`.

## Flow
- an app author reaches for the kit's ManifestTool to type a manifest (README says classifyTool lets an app test its own manifest)
- the type omits four fields the bridge emits and once used a side_effects word the core refuses
- proposal A: delete HostManifest/ManifestTool/ManifestReadable from types.ts and the barrel (0 consumers)
- proposal B: keep them and add a parity test reading manifest.py's dataclass fields

## Expected impact
Removes a contract fork that has already drifted once; measured as fields in manifest.py/gate.js manifestOf absent from the TS mirror (4 today) or as exported types with no consumer (3). Deleting breaks nothing in the tree (0 imports).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the TS manifest types either match the contract under a test or do not exist
Before: 3 exported manifest types, 0 consumers, 4 contract fields missing, no parity test
After: predicted: A - 0 fork types; B - 0 missing fields with a test that fails on the next drift
Method: probe - consumer and field counts are measured; choosing delete vs pin, and a parity test that reads Python from TS or TS from Python, sits outside this round's paths (tests/ or src/athena)
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
$ git grep -n 'ManifestTool\|HostManifest\b\|ManifestReadable' -- examples packages apps ':!examples/demo-kit/src/webmcp/types.ts' ':!**/.next/**'
examples/demo-kit/src/index.ts:21-25 (barrel only)
packages/athena-bridge/gate.js:117-135 manifestOf emits page_origin, origin_kind, transport_detected, tools[].inferred_from
examples/demo-kit/src/webmcp/types.ts ManifestTool/HostManifest: none of those four
instrument: for B: a tests/ parity test that extracts the HostManifest/ManifestTool field names from types.ts and compares them with manifest.py's dataclass fields (red today: 4 missing); for A: delete and run root pnpm typecheck plus the four example test suites
